GBOS Recreation Grants Timeline

July 1st: Grant Packets Ready

Mid-July: At least two consecutive weeks of posting on the City website and around
town.
        - GBOS announcement of Grant Process

August 3: Grant Packets Ready for Pick up

FRI September 18: Grant Application Deadline, to GBOS office by 3pm

Sept GBOS Meeting: Staff to announce request amounts to GBOS at regular monthly
meeting

September 28 6PM: Grant Presentation meeting
GBOS members receive applications and grant evaluation form, along with instructions
for evaluations. Members have until GBOS Meeting Oct 19 to complete their evaluations
and make recommendations for funding within budget.


October 19:  Regular GBOS meeting, the board makes determination on awarding the
grants and actually amounts to award to each grant
GBOS members announce their recommendation for funding per grant, within budget.
Amounts are averaged to produce the final recommendation from GBOS.

October 20-November
Staff requests grant revision forms completed by non-profits so that budgets match the
amount awarded by GBOS.

November: Grant funding is sent to Muni with GBOS overall budget request

January to March:  Grantee’s submit the past year Final Reports; Deadline mid-Feb
March to April: Grant contracts signed by grantees; contracts are sent to MOA for
processing

May to June: Grant money is dispersed by the Muni to the awarded Grantees

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:
Application for funding is competitive. The total amount of funding requested is expected to exceed the amount of money
available. A detailed application containing a comprehensive proposal of the project and realistic funding request is
essential.

Please review this information, including the attached criteria and process information sheets before starting the
application. The application forms are self-explanatory. Include all of the requested information or required
attachments.  If an item does not apply to your project, note “N/A” for that item. A checklist is attached.

One copy of your complete, typed (minimum font size 10) application must be received by 3:00PM on Friday,
September 18, 2026.

Grant requests will be announced at the September 21, 2026 GBOS regular meeting. A GBOS Work Session will be
scheduled to hear GVSA Non-Profit Recreation Grant Presentations. You or your representative is required to attend
this work session. You will be given approximately 5 minutes to present your application to GBOS, followed by Q&A
time from the public and the board. Additional discussion will take place during the October 19, 2026 GBOS Regular
meeting and a final vote will likely be held at that meeting.

Incomplete application or missed deadline will be grounds for rejection of the application.

Girdwood Valley Service Area
                     Parks & Recreation Non-Profit Recreation Organization
                                  Grant Funding Program

 The Girdwood Parks and Recreation Department strives to ensure that comprehensive and diverse recreation programs
 and activities are made available to the community. The objective of this grant program is to use tax funds collected in
 the Girdwood Valley Service Area (GVSA) to assist in providing a variety of quality recreation projects.

 How do we define recreation?
 Recreation:     Consists of leisure time activities that contribute to healthful living.
               Enhances participation and skill-building.
                     Instills positive personality characteristics.
              Expands one’s interests and increases quality of life.

 Eligible projects fall into one or more of the following categories:
       I.      Enable community members of Girdwood to participate in recreation activities. Grant funds will be
              specifically used to:
          A. Provide scholarships to individuals, or
           B.  Directly result in a quantifiable fee reduction to the participant.

       II.     Expand existing recreational opportunities. The grant funded project will fill a need in the
           community that:
          A. Cannot be met by the Municipality as effectively or efficiently, or
           B.  Is not currently being met by another agency in the community.

      III.     Foster new, innovative, unique projects. The grant funds will:
          A. Provide seed money for new projects not currently available in the GVSA
           B. Provide special recreational opportunity for the community

Restrictions on this Funding:
Below is a list of key restrictive parameters on funding, other restrictions may apply:
       I.     The organization must have obtained 501(c)3, 501(c)4 or 501(c)19 status as verified by a formal
             determination letter from the IRS. Applicants may also be fiscally sponsored projects, as long as the
               fiscal sponsor has a 501(c)3, 501(c)4 or 501(c)19 status. Grantee is responsible for completion of all
            requirements under this contract. Informal associations are not eligible for grants.

       II.     The organization must have been in operation in the GVSA for at least one year prior to application.

      III.    There are no guarantees of annual funding.

     IV.    This grant funding is subject to the availability of funds lawfully appropriated for disbursement.

    V.    The intent is to supplement the project, not to fund the project in total.  It should be noted that funding is
             provided, in full, within a reasonable period upon execution of the contract.

     VI.    Grants are for direct project expenses only, such as supplies, equipment or facility rental for project
               activities, project staff wages (to a limited degree), project travel expenses within the Anchorage area, etc.

VII.   Grant funds may not be used for general operating or administrative expenses of your organization, such as
            administrative personnel expenses, non-project space rent or utility costs, liability  insurance, office
             supplies, audit or legal fees, fund-raising expense, etc.

    VIII.   Recreation programming is the goal; grant funds are not to be used for construction activities or capital
           equipment, lobbying, or any political activity.

 Insurance Requirements for grant recipients:
  I.       Certificate of Insurance naming the Municipality of Anchorage as Additional Insured and Waiver of
         Subrogation must be in effect during the entire contract period. Additionally, programs that work with youth or
         other at-risk populations are required to carry sexual molestation coverage.

      Minimum Insurance Requirements:
          1      $500,000 Worker’s Compensation and Employer’s Liability as required by Alaska Law.
          2      Commercial Automobile Liability per occurrence in the amount of $500,000 single limit to
                      include: owned, hired and non-owned.
          3      Comprehensive General Liability in the amount of $1,000,000 combined single limit to  include:
                       a.  Premises operations
                     b.  Products and completed operations
                       c.  Blanket contractual
                     d.  Broad form property damage
                       e.  Independent contractors
                            f.  Personal injury coverage

  II.     Each policy of insurance required by this section shall provide or a faxed copy of insured’s cancellation notice,
         within two (2) business days of receipt, to the Municipality of Anchorage.

  III.    With the exception of Worker’s Compensation, each policy shall name the Municipality of Anchorage as an
          additional insured and the actual policy endorsement shall accompany each Certificate of Insurance.

 IV.    General liability and Automobile policies shall be endorsed to waive all rights of subrogation against the
         Municipality of Anchorage by reason of any payment made of claims under the above coverage. This policy
        endorsement should accompany each Certificate of Insurance.

Evaluation Criteria – The Grant Review Committee will evaluate your application based on:
I.      Purpose of the Project:
     What demonstrated community need is being met? What is the impact on the community if this project is not
      provided? What other programs/agencies exist to meet this need? How do they compare to this project?

II.     Management of the Project:
     Does your application show effective management of financial and human resources? Are there appropriate
       technical skills and knowledge of this program service? Is it fiscally responsible? Does it have a proven
        ability/track record?

III.    Community Support of Project:
      Are the following elements evident in your application? Strong participation, volunteer services, financial
       support from other funding sources such as private and corporate contributions, user fees, in-kind donations.

IV.     Specifics of Project:
       Target population – who benefits from your project? Is it cost-effective? Did you present a comprehensive
      concept and organized plan of action? Does it include measurable results? Is this a recreation-oriented project?

V.    Appearance:
       Application must be complete, concise and relevant. Applications in excess of 6 pages will be returned.

 1.​    Summarize the project you are proposing. Include primary goals and objectives.
 Four Valleys Community School (FVCS) provides year-round recreational, educational, and cultural

FVCS offers a wide range of opportunities based on the community's interests and needs, including indoor and

running, fitness and yoga, and other enrichment activities. FVCS partners with local individuals, instructors,
and organizations to provide these programs, and past funding has allowed us to compensate visiting
instructors for their time and expertise.

During the school year, most programming takes place after school and on weekends, providing accessible
opportunities for children, families, and adults. Summer programming expands to include day camps, evening
art events, and weekday and weekend outdoor activities for both youth and adults.

FVCS’s long-term goal is to provide a safe, welcoming environment where community members can learn,
recreate, connect, and contribute. We strive to offer a quality mix of programs that families can participate in
together while also creating opportunities for community members to share their time, skills, and volunteer
support.

FVCS also serves the community through events such as ourannual Sport Swap, a weekend event where
families and individuals can sell their gently used outdoor gear and find quality equipment at affordable
prices. In an outdoor-centered community like Girdwood, access to affordable gear can be a significant barrier
to participation. The Sport Swap keeps good equipment in circulation, makes outdoor recreation more
accessible, and gives FVCS another way to support the community beyond traditional classes and programs.


 2.​    What evaluation criteria will be used to determine if goals and objectives have been met? Be specific.
 FVCS evaluates the success of its programming through enrollment numbers, community engagement, and
 ongoing participant feedback. We closely track participation in classes and events, feedback from
 post-program participant surveys, and referrals from new instructors who bring different skills and ideas that
 can expand our program offerings.

Monthly budget check-ins provide another way to evaluate whether programming is meeting community
needs. By reviewing enrollment and program finances regularly, FVCS can identify which classes are
generating strong interest and which may need to be adjusted, replaced, or offered in a different format. This
allows us to respond rather than continue programs that do not meet the community's needs or interests.

FVCS strives to balance reliable, recurring programs with unique or seasonal offerings. While some programs
happen every year, we also introduce pop-up classes and one-time or occasional programs to keep the calendar

 3.​     Describe why the project to be funded under this proposal is needed and how it will benefit the
       community. Is this a new or existing project? Is there unmet need or population that will be served
        with this project?

Four Valleys Community School (FVCS) is entering its 46th year of serving the community as the primary
provider of after-school recreation, arts, and cultural activities in the Four Valleys. FVCS is also the only
locally focused organization providing outdoor recreation and arts programming specifically for residents of
Girdwood, Bird, Indian, Hope, and Portage during the summer months.

FVCS programs take place almost exclusively within the Four Valleys, allowing local families to access
opportunities close to home rather than traveling to Anchorage or farther away. This local access is especially
important for families without reliable transportation. When programs are offered within the community,
children and families can often walk or bike to participate, removing transportation as a barrier to
participation.

Local after-school programming is especially valuable for working families. Children can walk directly from
their classrooms into a safe, supervised environment where they can participate in recreational, educational,
and creative activities without requiring parents to make another trip across town. This creates a seamless
transition from the school day into meaningful after-school opportunities.

Keeping programs local also reduces the need for highway travel, which is especially important during the
winter months when road conditions can be unpredictable, and travel between communities can be difficult or
unsafe. By bringing recreation, arts, and enrichment opportunities directly to the communities we serve, FVCS
helps ensure that families have access to engaging activities year-round, regardless of transportation
challenges or seasonal conditions.



 4.​     Provide a brief history of your organization, especially as it relates to Girdwood Parks and
        Recreation.

Four Valleys Community School (FVCS) was established in 1980 and was initially funded entirely through
the Municipality of Anchorage (MOA) Parks and Recreation Department. FVCS operated under this model
until 1986, when MOA funding began to decrease, and Girdwood was no longer a municipal funding priority.
To keep local programming available, the community turned to the Girdwood Board of Supervisors (GBOS)
for financial support.

In 1988, community school organizations throughout Anchorage were absorbed into the Anchorage School
District (ASD), and FVCS continued operating under ASD until June 2004. As funding for community school
programs was continually reduced and ultimately eliminated, FVCS transitioned to independent nonprofit
status in 2006. This allowed the organization to continue providing programs under local control, focused on

serving the needs and interests of the Girdwood community.

Since becoming an independent nonprofit, FVCS has remained almost entirely community-driven and
community-supported. Today, FVCS provides a wide range of recreational, educational, and cultural
opportunities for people of all ages and financial abilities throughout the year. Our history reflects the
community's commitment to maintaining local opportunities and ensuring that residents have access to
meaningful activities close to home.
